_comment: Which GAS global services require which OAuth scope, for projects that declare an explicit oauthScopes list in appsscript.json. GAS only auto-detects required scopes when the manifest has NO oauthScopes key at all — the moment a project lists any scopes explicitly, it stops auto-detecting and grants exactly what's listed, so a used-but-undeclared scope fails silently at the API call site (this is exactly the bug this tool was built to catch, after it happened once during Round 3 reconciliation: UrlFetchApp was added without adding script.external_request). This table is NOT exhaustive — it covers the global objects actually used somewhere in this repo. Extend it if a project starts using a new advanced service.

_notes.Session: Only actually needs userinfo.email if the code calls Session.getActiveUser()/getEffectiveUser() and reads .getEmail(); Session.getScriptTimeZone() needs no scope. This tool flags any Session.* usage conservatively (may over-flag getScriptTimeZone() calls as needing the scope when they don't) — check.js documents this in its own output rather than silently guessing which method was called.
_notes.GmailApp: Narrowed from the single full-mailbox https://mail.google.com/ scope (least-privilege fix, also the prime suspect in a real live OAuth-consent-dialog crash — see leader-hub's git history around the appsscript.json change this note came from) to the two scopes leader-hub's EmailBridge.gs actually uses: gmail.readonly (scanHorizonLabel_() reads message subject/body, never modifies) and gmail.compose (createBragDraft_() creates drafts, never sends). checkOAuthScopes() requires ALL scopes listed here to be present (AND semantics, same as every other service in this map) — correct for the one real GmailApp consumer in this repo today, but not a general "any Gmail scope will do" statement: a future project calling GmailApp methods that send, modify, or delete (not just read/compose) would need a broader scope this list doesn't cover, and this map has no per-method granularity to catch that automatically — extend it (or add a project-specific override) if that ever happens rather than assuming this list already covers it.
